title: What If Earth Started Spinning Backward?

scenes.text: What if Earth spun the other way? The sun would rise in the west. That's the smallest change.
Today the equator moves at about 1,040 miles an hour. Reverse that, and the whole planet's weather has to rewire.
A climate simulation found that the Atlantic's great heat-carrying current would vanish, and a similar one would appear in the Pacific.
Winters in northwestern Europe would turn significantly colder, while new deserts would open in the southeastern United States and northern China.
Yet the world's deserts would shrink, from about 16 million square miles to about 12 million, as grasses and shrubs took over.
It would take thousands of years. A backward Earth wouldn't be a worse planet, just a very different one.

description:
What if Earth spun the other way?
A climate simulation found the Atlantic's heat current would vanish, Europe's winters would turn colder, and the world's deserts would shrink from 16 million to 12 million square miles.
What should we run through next?
